name: PT Lovina Beach Brewery Tbk

frontmatter.title: Lovina Beach Brewery: a Bali distiller priced as an event, not a business
frontmatter.summary: We initiate at SELL with a fundamental target of Rp4 against a traded price of Rp87. The recovery visible in the filed half year does not reach the equity: at the second-quarter exit run-rate SG&A consumes every rupiah of gross profit, the stand-alone DCF is worth less than nothing, and the shares price a change of control rather than the distillery.
thesis: The recovery is real but it does not reach the equity: revenue roughly doubled in 1H2026 against the whole of FY2025 and gross margin reached the mid-forties [S0], yet EBIT is still IDR-13.0bn in FY2026E because SG&A is IDR21.7bn.

The second quarter is the run-rate, not the first: 2Q26 revenue annualised at roughly twenty-one billion rupiah with a gross margin near twenty-six per cent [S0], and we price FY2026E from that exit rather than from an unsourced second-half recovery.

The cost structure is the investment case: SG&A was IDR29.3bn on IDR12.9bn of revenue and was still three quarters of sales in FY2023A at three times the volume [S0], so operating profit arrives only if revenue is rebuilt past the FY2023A base at a cost base near the current run-rate.
The ten-year DCF returns a negative enterprise value: the operating business is worth less than the cash it consumes, so the stand-alone equity is supported only by the 30 June 2026 net cash [S0].

The share price is not pricing the brewery: PT Barito Mas Sukses is negotiating the sale of 61.9% of the company to PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera [S2], and the stock more than doubled in October 2026 on that alone.

catalysts.event: Any disclosure of price, funding or tender-offer intention from PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera on the control block
FY2026 audited accounts: first full-year test of whether the second-quarter volume holds through the December quarter
Export shipment evidence into Japan, China, Singapore and the United States under the Asset Whale distribution agreement

blocks.text: **SELL, target Rp4, total return -95.5%** against the 6 November close of Rp87 [S0]. PT Lovina Beach Brewery is a single-site brewery and distillery in Bali selling craft beer, arak, whisky, soju and coconut-based drinks under Stark, Kaja, Libaron, Aja and Coco Bali through sub-distributors and export agents [S5][S8]. It listed in October 2023, raising IDR118.0bn with 1,180 million shares offered [S6], built a plant with IDR66.3bn of capex [S0], and then watched revenue fall from IDR39.3bn to IDR12.9bn in two years [S0].

The variant view is not that the recovery is fake. It is that the recovery is already visible in the filed half year and still does not reach the equity. We price FY2026E revenue at IDR23.9bn and gross margin at 36.5% [S0], which is arithmetic from the quarterly path rather than a forecast: the first half's annualised run-rate, the second quarter alone, and the exit quarter's gross margin near twenty-six per cent [S0]. An earlier draft carried a higher base because it assumed the second half would recover; no archived source supports that, so we do not.

What the market pays for is the 61.9% control block that PT Barito Mas Sukses is negotiating to sell to PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera, a buyer that separately holds 15.1% of the listed out-of-home advertiser DOOH [S2]. That is an event, and events are not modelled here. The operating case, transparently stated, is that at the current cost base the company earns nothing: the ten-year DCF returns a negative enterprise value, and the positive rupiah in our blend come entirely from the two cross-checks, not from the brewery.

Two things move the value. First, SG&A intensity: if the fixed distribution and promotion base does not fall as a share of revenue, the company never earns, because gross margin cannot cover it — FY2023A proves the point, when three times today's revenue still produced negative EBIT [S0]. Second, the export channel: a 15.0% stake sold to Singapore's Asset Whale Pte Ltd in July 2025 came with distribution management and international regulatory support [S3], and the company says it is expanding whisky and Coco Bali exports into Japan, China, Singapore and the United States [S8]. We credit that ramp in the forecast and still land at a fraction of the price.

The company produces and distributes alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages from Bali. The portfolio is wide for the size of the revenue line: craft beer under Stark, a malt-based spirit under Kaja, whisky under Libaron, arak under Arak De'Wan and Arak Legong, soju under Aja, plus flavoured liqueurs and coconut nectar lines sold as Coco Bali [S5][S8]. Production runs through the company and its subsidiary PT Lovina Industri Sukses, and the brands are sold domestically through a distributor network with Jakarta covering the western islands and Bali the centre and east [S5], and through sub-distributors to hotels, outlets, restaurants, bars and supermarkets [S0]. The company employs 30.0 people, which tells you the cost base is materials, freight, trade spend and third-party distribution rather than payroll [S0].

That channel mix is the business's defining feature and its problem. Sales to hotels, bars and restaurants in Bali are tourism-linked; sales through modern retail carry listing and promotion costs that sit in SG&A. Revenue peaked at IDR39.3bn in FY2023A, the year of the listing and the plant build, then fell to IDR18.9bn and IDR12.9bn [S0] — a collapse large enough that the FY2025A gross margin of 3.9% is better read as under-absorption of a plant sized for far more volume than as a pricing failure.

The strategy the company describes is export-led: use the Balinese provenance as the differentiator, sell into premium on-trade channels abroad, and let the domestic distributor network carry the fixed cost of the home market [S5][S8]. The disclosed export plan is concrete on geography and silent on economics: the company names Japan, China, Singapore and the United States as target markets and describes agave from Nusa Penida and local fruit as the product story [S8], but it does not disclose volumes, realised prices or the trade spend required to hold a listing in a foreign hotel group. We treat both as open questions rather than assumptions in the company's favour.

The company is a challenger, not a leader. Ownership is concentrated: PT Barito Mas Sukses held the 61.9% block now under negotiation [S2], and management is unchanged through the transaction, with Bona Budhisurya as President Director and Anna Vanessa as Finance Director [S5]. The plant at Banyuning in Buleleng is the only manufacturing asset that matters and it is already built [S8], so the marginal cost of incremental volume is materials and freight, not capital — which is why the volume recovery should show up in gross margin before it shows up in EBIT. It has not yet, because the SG&A line is large and sticky.

Indonesian spirits distribution runs through layers of sub-distributors because a producer selling direct to tens of thousands of outlets across an archipelago cannot fund the receivables. Each layer takes a margin and each layer must be incentivised, which is why a premium brand can carry a high gross margin and still lose money at the operating line. Bali is a tourist economy first, so on-premise volume tracks arrivals rather than national consumption, and the island's high season concentrates demand into a few months of the year.

The addressable market is small and heavily taxed. Brewed and distilled alcohol in Indonesia sits inside an excise and licensing regime that shapes what can be sold where, and the highest-proof categories where the whisky and arak margin sits carry the tightest retail-sale restrictions. We have not archived the current excise tariff or the retail-restriction regulation, so we label this industry structure as analyst judgment rather than a sourced fact; it is a live policy exposure and the report does not quantify it. What is sourced is narrower and still useful: the exchange issued an unusual-market-activity notice when the share price detached from the business in 2023 [S7], and the company itself describes an increasingly competitive global market for its products [S5].

The company competes in the premium end of that market, where the buyer is a hotel, a bar or a specialist retailer rather than a household, so the relevant measure of scale is on-premise penetration in Bali and in the export cities it is entering, not national share [S5]. Lovina's revenue is a rounding error against a national brewer, so it has no cost advantage and no shelf-space leverage; its only lever is price and provenance. The claim that Bali on-premise distribution is contested by imported spirits at higher price points and by the national brewer's beer portfolio is our reading of the competitive structure, not something the archived sources state, and we flag it as such.

The structural drivers we track are three. Tourist arrivals into Bali set the on-premise volume base, and the company does not control them. Excise and retail policy set the price ceiling on the highest-proof products, which is where the arak and whisky margin sits. And the export channel is a regulatory and distribution problem rather than a demand problem, which is precisely what the Asset Whale agreement was bought to solve [S3]. None of the three is a market-share story, and that is why we do not value the company on a multiple of national category growth.

Growth has to come from two places the company can control. The first is export, where the regulatory risk is foreign rather than domestic: the company names Japan, China, Singapore and the United States as the markets it is opening for whisky and Coco Bali [S8]. The second is premium mix, where the cultural positioning — Balinese ingredients, agave from Nusa Penida, chemical-free distillation — is a differentiation claim rather than a cost advantage [S8]. Neither is evidenced by a contract or a volume commitment, and we do not treat the company's own account of its distribution progress as independent verification.

The moat assessment is unflattering. There are no switching costs on a bottle, no network effect, and distribution density in Bali is contested, in our judgment, by imports and by the national brewer's beer portfolio. Brand is the only candidate moat and it is not evidenced by pricing power: a gross margin that fell to a low single digit and a revenue line that fell by two thirds in two years is the opposite of a brand defended through a downturn [S0].

The five forces read badly on buyer power, because sub-distributors and hotel groups can switch supplier on a listing cycle, and on rivalry, because imports and the national brewer both price against the same shelf [S5]. They read only mildly well on new entry, because excise licensing and a large plant are real barriers, and on substitutes, because the category has few. Our conclusion is that the company has a brand asset worth defending but no mechanism that makes the defence compound, which under the house compounder card rules out a no-fade DCF: excess returns have to fade toward the cost of capital, and in this case they do not exist yet to fade.

Regulation is a live exposure rather than a footnote. Excise changes pass through to the retail price of exactly the products carrying the company's margin, and the exchange will intervene when the share price detaches from the business, as the 2023 unusual-market-activity notice shows [S7]. We do not carry a specific excise increase in the forecast because we have not archived the tariff schedule; the exposure sits in the bear case as a qualitative risk rather than a modelled shock.

The history is one story told three ways. Revenue went IDR30.9bn, IDR39.3bn, IDR18.9bn, IDR12.9bn [S0] while the asset base was rebuilt: capex of IDR66.3bn in FY2023A left IDR62.8bn of net fixed assets, and equity rose to IDR153.8bn on the IPO proceeds [S0]. Operating losses followed revenue down, with EBIT of IDR-28.8bn and a net loss of IDR-21.3bn [S0]. The FY2023A profit of IDR11.0bn was not an operating result: EBIT was negative and a non-operating gain carried the P&L [S0].

The quarterly path is the whole forecast, and the data pack's quarterly series has to be read carefully because the 2026 second-quarter line is cumulative. The first quarter was the strong one, the second quarter alone was roughly five billion of revenue at a gross margin near twenty-six per cent, down thirty-seven per cent quarter on quarter and down thirty points of margin [S0]. Annualising the second quarter gives an exit run-rate of about twenty-one billion rupiah at that margin. That is the number we build from, not the first half's average.

Our FY2026E revenue of IDR23.9bn therefore prices the first half as filed and the second half flat on the second quarter's run-rate; it is deliberately below the flat-second-half arithmetic of roughly twice the half-year total that an earlier draft stated, because reaching that figure would require third and fourth quarter revenue about thirty per cent above the quarter that actually printed, and we have no source for that recovery. Gross margin of 36.5% follows mechanically: the first half's mid-forties average is diluted by carrying the second half at the exit margin. The path then grows 35.0% in FY2027E and decelerates to 10.0% in FY2030E, reaching IDR48.9bn on the company's export plan [S8], with gross margin grinding to 45.0% as volume rebuilds over the same plant.

Costs are where the model does the work, and the change from the first draft is deliberate. SG&A of IDR21.7bn in FY2026E is the annualised 1H2026 run-rate, and we hold it in absolute terms, rising gently to IDR24.5bn with nominal inflation [S0]. It no longer falls in absolute terms between forecast years, which was the contradiction the red team found; the ratio falls from 91.0% to 50.0% only because revenue roughly doubles. We did not source any cost programme, headcount plan or distributor-term change, and we do not assume one: the observed cut from FY2025A's IDR29.3bn to the 1H2026 run-rate is already in the base, and everything beyond it would be invention. Even so, EBIT is IDR-13.0bn in FY2026E, IDR-8.4bn in FY2027E and only reaches IDR-2.4bn in FY2030E; EBITDA turns positive in FY2030E at IDR0.8bn.

The owner-earnings bridge makes the same point without the DCF. In FY2026E, EBIT of IDR-13.0bn plus D&A of IDR3.0bn less capex of IDR0.7bn less the working-capital movement of IDR-0.3bn gives free cash flow to the firm of IDR-10.5bn; by FY2030E the same bridge gives IDR-2.4bn plus IDR3.3bn less IDR3.2bn less IDR0.9bn, or IDR-2.9bn. Owner earnings never turn positive in the forecast, which is the arithmetic behind the SELL [S0].

Cash is the constraint and the clock. Operating cash flow was negative in FY2025A, working capital of 46.0% of revenue is beginning to absorb cash as volume returns, and free cash flow to the firm stays negative through the decade [S0]. The FY2025A cash balance of IDR38.4bn had fallen to a lower interim level by 30 June 2026 [S0], and the model shows it falling further to IDR29.6bn in FY2026E and below twenty billion by FY2027E. Debt of IDR3.8bn at the FY2025 close is immaterial and slightly lower at the interim balance sheet [S0]; no new facility is assumed, and the company has not drawn term debt since the IPO.

**Earnings-quality flags.** The usual accruals ratio is meaningless here because both numerator and denominator are negative, so we use the divergence screen instead. Trade receivables and inventory together stood at IDR11.3bn at the FY2025 close against revenue of IDR12.9bn, roughly two thirds of a year of sales, with inventory alone against COGS of IDR12.4bn [S0]; receivables have not outgrown revenue because revenue collapsed, but the absolute balance is large for a business this size and we flag collection risk. The FY2023A profit of IDR11.0bn came from a non-operating gain while EBIT was negative [S0]. On the IDX regime screens, the stock carries a prior unusual-market-activity notice and a 200.0% post-listing surge [S7]; free float is 22.2% [S0]. No manipulation-class flag is confirmed, but the disclosure record is thin.

D&A needs one sentence of its own because the red team was right about it. The filed run-rate is about IDR3.0bn a year against IDR62.8bn of net plant, and our forecast uses that run-rate rather than the higher figure in the first draft [S0]. D&A is added back in FCFF, so the change moves EBIT, the earnings screen and the tax line — it does not move the DCF's cash flows at all. Where it does matter is the book value behind the P/B leg: the plant that earns a terminal EBIT margin of a few per cent sits in equity at its cost, and an impairment to earning value would cut book rather than cash flow. We carry that consequence in the risk section rather than in the base case, because no impairment has been announced.

Our forecast is not a recovery story, and it is important to say so plainly. It is the last filed quarter carried forward at the company's own growth plan, with the cost base the company actually reported. If the second half recovers, the numbers are better than this; if it does not, they are worse. The forecast does not assume either [S0].

The method set fits the business, not the sector, and the denominators are disclosed because the red team rightly objected that the first draft hid them. The primary is a ten-year FCFF DCF at eighty per cent of the weight: it is the only method that prices the cash burn, and it is forward from FY2026E. The weights are not the industry default and the substitution is deliberate: a P/E leg is unusable because EPS is negative in every forecast year of this model [S0], so the two ten-per-cent legs are an asset floor (P/B at the peer median) and a scale check (EV/Sales), and neither carries enough weight to drive the target. The EV/Sales cross-check at ten per cent is applied by the engine to FY2025A revenue of IDR12.9bn, which is the trough year, because that is the last audited sales line. At the same 0.9 multiple on FY2026E revenue of IDR23.9bn the enterprise value would be only about twenty-one billion rupiah, smaller than the 30 June 2026 net cash [S0]; after adding that cash back the leg is about four and a half rupiah a share, higher than the Rp4 the engine prints on trough revenue, not negative. We keep the trough denominator anyway, because it is the only audited sales line and because pricing the recovery year would assume the recovery holds; if the second-half run-rate fails, FY2026E revenue is the wrong base and the higher leg flatters the cross-check. The P/B cross-check at ten per cent is struck on the 30 June 2026 interim book of the data pack [S0]. Cost of equity is 12.5% and WACC 12.5%, built from the IDR risk-free rate net of the sovereign default spread plus one beta unit of the mature ERP and country risk premium; debt is de minimis so WACC sits just below COE.

The DCF result is the story. The engine returns an enterprise value of IDR-40.2bn — negative — because ten years of negative free cash flow, discounted at 12.5%, outweigh the terminal value, which is itself only 23.9% of that enterprise value. After the interim net cash the equity value is negative and the engine reports a per-share value of Rp0. We do not smooth that away: the correct reading is that the stand-alone operating business is worth less than nothing, the cash is being consumed by it, and a rational owner would sooner close the plant than fund the loss. The DCF is therefore really a cash-minus-burn calculation, exactly as the red team described the first draft, and the change is that the burn is now large enough to consume the cash rather than merely to reduce it.

The book-value cross-check is the one place where the first draft fell over, and it is rebuilt. The multiple is the peer median of 1.6, not the average of the peer median and an "own five-year average". That label was wrong on its face: the company listed in October 2023, so there are only three annual observations, and the third was taken at a December 2025 share price several times what this model says the business is worth. A high multiple on shrunken book is a distress reading, not an anchor, and averaging it with the peer median imported the speculation into the target. Using the peer median on the interim book gives Rp17 per share; the old own-history blend gave more than three times that and supplied four fifths of the target. On a negative return on equity the peer median is already generous, and we say so.

The divergence is now resolved rather than averaged. The earlier book leg diverged from the DCF by more than a thousand per cent, and the report described that as "informative". It was not informative; it was the target. We have cut the book weight to ten per cent, kept the DCF at eighty, and disclosed the split: every rupiah of the positive per-share value in the blend comes from the two cross-checks, because the DCF contributes zero. The book leg is a ceiling on what an asset buyer might pay for the shell, not a stand-alone value, and we present it as such. With the own-history observation excluded, the book leg is Rp17; including it would restore a target an order of magnitude above the cash flows, which is precisely the circularity we have removed.
The cross-checks do not rescue the price.
Book value is the one positive denominator and even at the peer median it is worth Rp17; the sales check is worth Rp4 on trough revenue.

The sensitivity grid is flat where it matters: the DCF reads Rp0 at every one of the twenty-five WACC and terminal-growth nodes, because the enterprise value is negative before discounting and the engine floors the per-share value at zero — no plausible cost of capital turns a negative cash-flow stream into value. The target grid moves only from Rp2 to under three rupiah across an eight-point revenue-growth range and a four-point gross-margin range, and almost all of that movement comes from the book and sales legs rather than the primary method. That is the signature of a valuation that is cash and burn rather than a growing perpetuity; the operating business is not doing DCF work, and we state that rather than dress it up.

What the price implies is the crux. At Rp87 the market capitalisation is 932,799,693,894.0 on FY2026E revenue of IDR23.9bn [S0]: an enterprise value of roughly thirty-eight times forward sales, or about seventy times FY2025A revenue, and one that no margin path in this model fills. The reverse DCF did not run — the price is not bracketed, meaning the implied value sits outside the solver's range rather than at a different discount rate — and we say that rather than claim a result we do not have. The implied exit test is equally unforgiving, and the terminal arithmetic says why. The four per cent terminal growth is funded by capex of IDR4.0bn plus a working-capital build of IDR0.9bn against D&A of IDR4.0bn — roughly one billion rupiah of net reinvestment — while NOPAT on terminal EBIT of IDR-1.8bn is negative after tax. The reinvestment rate therefore cannot be struck against a positive NOPAT, and ROIIC on the incremental capital is negative: the growth adds cost rather than value, which is why the terminal value is itself negative and 23.9% of a negative enterprise value. An exit EV/EBIT is undefined at both ends of the test — negative at entry on FY2026E EBIT of IDR-13.0bn and negative in the terminal year — so no exit multiple can bridge the entry price, because the denominator fails before any multiple is chosen. The market is valuing the 61.9% block under negotiation [S2], and until an offer price is disclosed there is no way to test that number. Our target is therefore explicitly a stand-alone value.

The largest downside risk is that the second-quarter deterioration does not reverse. It is one quarter, the December quarter is the seasonal peak for on-premise in Bali, and a restocking effect after a collapsed year looks identical to a recovery in a single report. Likelihood high, impact high. The bear case prices exactly this: growth eight points lower, gross margin seven points lower and SG&A eleven points higher as a share of revenue, which takes the cost ratio toward four fifths of sales at the FY2027E revenue base [S0].

The second risk is that the cost structure does not bend. SG&A at three quarters of sales in FY2023A shows the company can carry a large revenue base and still lose money [S0]; if the fixed distribution and promotion spend is stickier than we model, the loss years extend and the cash pile is consumed. Likelihood medium, impact high. The base case already holds SG&A flat in real terms, so this risk is only partly in the bear.

The third risk is funding and dilution. With free cash flow negative through the forecast and the conservative cash position at 30 June 2026 [S0], an equity raise at a discount to book is a live possibility and would dilute per-share value further. The scenario layer does not carry the issuance: the bear target is therefore an upper bound on the bear, not a full account of it, and we say so rather than pretend the arithmetic covers it. The same is true of the plant: an impairment to earning value would cut the book equity behind the P/B leg and remove several rupiah per share from the blend, and no scenario carries that either. Both omissions work against our own call, which is the honest direction for a SELL to be wrong in.

The fourth risk is the control transaction, and it cuts both ways. A negotiation is not a sale: PT Barito Mas Sukses is a seller in discussion with PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera for 61.9% [S2], and the price has already discounted a deal. If it fails, the stock returns to stand-alone valuation, which is close to our target. If it completes at a premium, our target is irrelevant — a tender offer at a negotiated price would override any fundamental value, and the operating-only bull therefore carries no tender-offer weight. We describe that as event risk rather than folding it into the base case.

Fifth, regulation: excise changes and retail-sale restrictions hit the highest-margin categories first, and the exchange has already issued an unusual-market-activity notice on this name [S7]. Sixth, governance: a controlling block changing hands to a buyer whose main listed vehicle is an out-of-home advertiser [S2] raises the question of what the brewery is for, and we cannot answer it from the disclosure. A seventh risk is dilution by structure rather than by operating failure: a change of control can be followed by an asset injection priced in new shares, and the buyer's other listed vehicle has been active in acquisitions [S2]. We cannot model that without terms, and we do not.

The scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers, with the base at 45% and the bear and bull at 30% and 25%. Base and bear land at the same value, Rp2 and Rp2, and that is not a modelling error: the DCF is already floored at zero, so there is no operating value left for a harsher case to remove. The bear's additional downside — dilution and impairment — is outside the engine. The bull, at Rp9, is the only case in which the operating business acquires positive value; it requires the export ramp to rebuild volume and SG&A to fall as a share of sales part-way back toward the FY2022A structure. Its gross margin is shocked by the same seven points as the bear, which lifts the long-run level halfway from the base path to the FY2023A actual earned on the same plant, and we stop there because no archived source quantifies the freight and rebate of the export channel [S0][S5]. Even then the target is Rp4 and the call is SELL. The SELL survives every scenario, including a hundred per cent bull weight, which is the test the red team set.

Signposts that would change the view: two consecutive quarters of revenue above the 1H2026 run rate with gross margin sustained; SG&A falling below half of sales; a disclosed tender-offer price; and any asset injection announced alongside the change of control.

Ownership is the story. PT Barito Mas Sukses held 61.9% of the shares, 6,633.4 million shares, and is in negotiation to sell the block to PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera [S2]. Free float is 22.2% and institutions hold 15.9% [S0], so the register is closed enough that the price is set by a small traded float. We correct an earlier overstatement here: three-month daily traded value clears the house liquidity threshold [S0], so this is not an illiquid stock; it is a liquid stock whose price is driven by an event, which is a different and more relevant risk. The house liquidity schedule therefore applies no discount, and the bridge does not carry one.

The transaction is disclosed through information disclosure to the exchange, which is the correct channel, but the terms are not: no price, no funding, no post-closing plan [S2]. A second strategic holder arrived in July 2025 when 15.0% of the shares went to Singapore's Asset Whale Pte Ltd alongside a distribution and regulatory-support agreement [S3]. Related-party flows between the producer and its sub-distributor network are not disclosed in the material we could archive, and we flag that as an open item rather than clearing it.

The dividend record is empty: no distribution since the 2023 listing [S0], and none is possible until accumulated losses are absorbed. The board is small and family-anchored, with a President Director and Finance Director in executive roles and an independent commissioner [S5]. The auditor and opinion could not be verified from the archived sources, and we disclose that as a gap in the evidence base rather than assert a clean audit.

ESG exposures are specific. Alcohol carries product-harm and marketing-restriction risk in a majority-Muslim market, the plant is a water and effluent user in Bali, and the growth claim rests on local sourcing and cultural heritage, which differentiates only if it survives audit [S5][S8]. Governance is where we would spend the next research cycle: the beneficial owners behind both sides of the block, and any pledge against it.

The near catalyst is the control transaction: disclosure of a price, a funding source or a tender-offer intention from PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera re-prices the equity immediately [S2]. The operating catalyst is the December quarter, because a recovery that does not hold through the seasonal peak is a restocking effect rather than a recovery. The FY2026 audited accounts are the first full-year test, and they are also the point at which the missing LK evidence base would be filled.

Between updates we monitor four numbers: quarterly revenue against the exit run-rate that sets FY2026E; gross profit as a share of sales, which must stay near the mid-forties to keep the recovery alive; SG&A as a share of sales, which must fall through the fifties; and the interim cash balance, which is the clock on the whole thesis. Exports are the swing factor and the company's own disclosure is the only source we have on them [S8]. We would also treat any announced equity issuance as a change to the per-share arithmetic rather than as noise.

bear.narrative: The 1H2026 volume recovery is a restocking and export-sample effect that does not repeat and the 2Q26 exit margin of 26.1% is the true run-rate [S0]. The export channel carries more freight and rebate than domestic sales, so gross margin stalls, while SG&A is held at the 1H2026 absolute run-rate and revenue disappoints, pushing the ratio toward four fifths of sales. The cash balance is consumed and, with no committed facility, the company would need external equity at a discount to book; the scenario arithmetic does not carry an issuance, so this bear target understates the dilution rather than overstating it. A plant impairment would also cut the book value behind the P/B leg.

bull.narrative: The export ramp lands: whisky and Coco Bali exports into Japan, China, Singapore and the United States [S8] through the Asset Whale distribution agreement [S3] rebuild volume past the FY2023A revenue base on a premium mix, and SG&A per rupiah of sales falls part-way back toward the FY2022A structure as the fixed base is spread over more revenue. Gross margin is shocked by the same seven points as the bear, which takes the long-run level to 52% - halfway between the 45% base and the 62.7% FY2023A actual earned on the same plant [S0], and short of it because no archived source quantifies the freight and rebate of the export channel, so we carry that cost as judgment rather than assume the domestic peak margin [S5][S8]. This is an operating-only bull: a change of control and any tender offer are event risk in section 5 and carry no weight here.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +85% is arithmetic from the filed quarterly path, not a forecast: revenue was Rp13.48bn in 1H2026 and the second quarter alone was Rp5.18bn, so a second half priced at the 2Q26 exit run-rate gives roughly Rp23.8bn for the year [S0]. We do not assume a second-half recovery: the flat-second-half figure of Rp27bn that a first draft carried would need 3Q-4Q revenue 30% above the quarter that actually printed, and no archived source supports that. FY2027E +35%, FY2028E +20%, FY2029E +15% and FY2030E +10% are the export ramp the company says it is executing - it is expanding whisky and Coco Bali exports into Japan, China, Singapore and the United States [S8], supported by a 15% strategic stake sold to Singapore's Asset Whale Pte Ltd for market research, distribution management and international regulatory compliance [S3] - decelerating to the house nominal growth path. Long-run growth is 4.0%, the house IDR terminal rate, below the long-run nominal GDP of the geography.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The FY2025A printed margin of 3.9% [S0] is a fixed-cost absorption trough, not the economics of the plant: gross margin was already 44.3% in 1H2026 on Rp13.48bn of revenue [S0] as volume came back over the same asset base. FY2026E is 36.5%, not the 44.3% half-year average, because the second quarter is carried at its own 26.1% exit margin (2Q26 gross profit of Rp1.35bn on Rp5.18bn of revenue) and the second half is priced flat on that quarter [S0]; the earlier 42% assumption implicitly assumed a second-half margin recovery that the filing does not support. FY2027E-FY2030E 43-45% is a partial recovery toward the pre-collapse structure of the same brands as volume rebuilds over the fixed plant, which earned a 67% gross margin on Rp30.9bn of revenue in FY2022A [S0]. We do not assume a full return to FY2022: the export and sub-distributor channel carries more freight and rebate than the FY2022 domestic mix.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: no driver deck prices malt, glass, molasses or freight, the four inputs that carry a brewery-distillery cost base, so a link to the agricultural or coal decks would be an invented sensitivity rather than a modelled one [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Consequential on link1_share being zero; there is no indexed input to pass through, so the pass-through parameter has no effect on the forecast [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Held at zero for the same reason as link 1: the company buys malt, glass and molasses on contract and sells premium spirits, so the deck-priced soft commodities in this house's coverage do not transmit into its cost of goods [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Consequential on link2_share being zero; no indexed input exists to pass through, so the parameter does not move the forecast [S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: SG&A was Rp29.3bn on Rp12.9bn of revenue in FY2025A (227%) [S0] and Rp10.9bn on Rp13.5bn in 1H2026 (81%) [S0]; at FY2023A's much larger Rp39.3bn revenue it was Rp29.6bn (75%) [S0]. The line is dominated by fixed distribution, listing and promotion costs. We hold it in absolute terms at the 1H2026 run-rate of roughly Rp21.7bn a year, rising about 4% a year with nominal wages, rather than letting it fall to Rp20.4bn in FY2027E as an earlier draft did: the level is the latest filed actual, and the company has already cut SG&A from Rp29.3bn in FY2025A to the Rp21.7bn run-rate, so no further reduction is assumed. The ratio therefore falls only because revenue rises; we do not return the ratio to FY2022A's 22% because the sub-distributor and export model carries more selling cost than the FY2022 own-distribution base [S5].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held in absolute terms near Rp3bn a year, the run-rate the 1H2026 filing implies (Rp1.48bn of D&A in the half) [S0], against Rp59.2bn of net fixed assets at 30 June 2026 [S0]. That is a 5% depreciation rate on a plant commissioned in FY2023 when capex was Rp66.3bn [S0]. The earlier Rp4.07bn assumption was above every filed observation; we now use the filed run-rate. D&A is added back in FCFF, so the change moves EBIT and the earnings screen, not the DCF, except through tax.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The Rp66.3bn brewery was built in FY2023A [S0]; FY2024A and FY2025A capex were Rp2.96bn and Rp0.15bn [S0], so what remains is maintenance and small line extensions behind new products [S8]. FY2026E 3.0% of revenue rising to 6.7% by FY2030E allows for bottling and canning capacity and cold chain as exports scale. The terminal ratio is set equal to terminal D&A (6.7% of revenue) so that a business growing 4% a year is not modelled as growing while its asset base shrinks: capex below depreciation at positive growth is an internal inconsistency, not a valuation assumption. The path stays well below the 61.9% average of the build years that the engine's default would have carried forward indefinitely.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A working capital was 87% of revenue only because the denominator collapsed: receivables of Rp8.25bn and inventory of Rp4.58bn sat against Rp12.9bn of sales [S0]. At FY2023A's scale the same balance-sheet lines were 46% of revenue [S0], and that is the ratio we carry, tightening to 40% as export and sub-distributor terms shorten. Carrying the 87% trough ratio would charge the recovery for a working-capital intensity the company has never had at normal volume.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: No tax is paid while the accumulated losses of the FY2024A-FY2026E run are carried forward: the company booked a tax credit of Rp5.43bn on a Rp26.76bn pre-tax loss in FY2025A [S0]. We step the rate up to 10% in FY2029E and 15% in FY2030E as the losses are absorbed rather than jumping to the 22% statutory rate the year the P&L turns, and use the statutory rate in the long run.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Debt is only Rp3.5bn against Rp111.9bn of equity at 30 June 2026 [S0]; the implied rate on the FY2023A-FY2025A average balance was 9.4%, and 9.0% is used forward on the assumption that working-capital facilities reprice with the policy rate.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Rp32.7bn of cash at 30 June 2026 [S0] earned an implied 5.7% on the FY2023A-FY2025A average balance; 5.5% is carried forward on time deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new facility is announced. The company is equity-funded and has not drawn term debt since the IPO proceeds of Rp118bn landed [S6]; we do not invent a refinancing.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the FY2023A pbt of Rp11.85bn against an EBIT of -Rp4.93bn [S0] came from a Rp39.75bn non-operating gain that the pack does not explain, and we do not carry an unexplained one-off into a forecast.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: The minority balance sheet interest is Rp0.06bn against Rp111.9bn of equity [S0], so the share of profit is set at nil and the subsidiary PT Lovina Industri Sukses is treated as wholly attributable in practice.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no dividend since listing in October 2023 [S0] and has accumulated losses of the FY2024A-FY2025A run to absorb before any distribution is legally possible.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or warrant exercise is live: the 3.24bn Series I warrants issued at the IPO expired on 9 October 2024 [S6]. The 10,721.8m shares therefore stay constant, and any future equity raise is treated as a risk in section 5 rather than a modelled dilution.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House IDR terminal rate of 4.0%, below long-run nominal GDP for Indonesia and consistent with a premium spirits franchise in a market where per-capita consumption is the growth driver rather than share gain; the reporting currency and data pack are the anchor for the rate [S0].

challenges.section: Investment summary / 2. Industry overview / 5. Bull scenario
challenges.challenge: The summary, section 2, the bull-scenario narrative and the revenue_growth basis all state a 'first whisky shipment' into 'five-star hotels and bars' and cite [S3]. S3 (wartaekonomi, 2,452 chars) contains zero occurrences of whisky, Libarron, hotel, bintang, pengiriman or ekspor; it says only 'peluncuran global portofolio produk terbaru' and names Japan, the United States and China as target markets. A named value driver is supported by a source that does not say it.
challenges.answer: Struck the unsourced first-shipment and five-star-hotel claim from the summary, section 2, the bull narrative and the revenue-growth basis. Archived S8 (merdeka, 27 Dec 2025), which states whisky and Coco Bali exports target Japan, China, Singapore and the United States; the ramp is now cited to S8 with no shipment date or channel claimed.

challenges.challenge: The 1H2026 figures are cumulative: 2026Q1 revenue Rp8.29bn / gross profit Rp4.63bn (55.8%) and 1H Rp13.48bn / Rp5.98bn (44.3%), so 2Q26 alone was Rp5.18bn / Rp1.35bn, a 26.1% gross margin - revenue -37% q/q and margin -30pp q/q. The report instead says FY2026E 42% 'holds the 1H2026 actual less a weaker first quarter'; the first quarter was the strong one. And FY2026E revenue of Rp29.04bn is 7.7% above the flat-second-half arithmetic its own basis states ('near Rp27bn', 2 x 13.48 = 26.96), i.e. the model needs 2H26 of Rp15.56bn (+15% h/h) after a -37% quarter plus a Q3/Q4 margin recovery to reach 42%. Neither is sourced or disclosed.
challenges.answer: FY2026E rebuilt from the quarterly path: 1H2026 revenue of Rp13.48bn and 2Q26 alone of Rp5.18bn at a 26.1% gross margin are stated in sections 3 and 5; the model prices the second half flat on the 2Q26 exit (revenue Rp23.9bn, gross margin 36.5%) instead of the unsourced flat-half figure, and the reversal is disclosed.

challenges.challenge: The P/B leg is 20% of the weight but supplies Rp10.72 of the Rp13.21 blend (P/B value Rp53.6/share against a DCF of Rp3.02). Its 5.135x multiple is the average of a 1.587x peer median and an 'own five-year average' that cannot exist: own_history pbv has n=3 (FY2023A 3.56x, FY2024A 3.89x, FY2025A 18.60x, mean 8.68x) because the company listed in October 2023, and the mean is dominated by the December 2025 observation at Rp202, a price this DCF says is about 22x fair value. An 18.6x reading taken on shrunken book is a distress multiple, not a valuation anchor. Applying 2.4x the peer median to a company with -17% ROE and negative FCFF recycles the speculation into the target, and the report never discloses the multiple or its basis.
challenges.answer: FATAL fixed. P/B is now the peer median 1.586x at a 10% weight, replacing the non-existent own five-year average; the report states the multiple and its basis, corrects the label to the three annual observations, explains why the December 2025 observation is excluded, and shows the peer-median book leg against the old own-history blend.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'Our target is therefore explicitly a stand-alone value', but 81% of the target is the P/B leg whose own-history mean is a speculative-era market multiple (18.6x at Rp202 in December 2025), so the target is partly marked at the price the report says cannot be tested. Separately, coe_basis states illiquidity is 'charged once through the house discount schedule in the valuation bridge', while the bridge applies a 0.0% liquidity discount. On a 22.2% float with a live 61.87% block negotiation, both statements cannot be true.
challenges.answer: coe_basis amended: the house liquidity schedule applies a zero haircut because three-month ADTV clears its top threshold, the bridge carries no discount and we no longer claim one. Section 4 discloses that every rupiah of positive per-share value comes from the two cross-checks because the DCF is zero; section 6 corrects the speculation-versus-liquidity line.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E opex is Rp20.39bn at revenue Rp39.21bn, which is Rp9.2bn (31%) below FY2023A's actual Rp29.58bn at essentially the same revenue (Rp39.28bn), with no cost programme, headcount plan or distributor-term change cited for the cut. The line also falls in absolute terms from FY2026E to FY2027E (21.78 to 20.39) while revenue grows 35%, which directly contradicts the section 3 sentence that SG&A 'does not fall in absolute terms through the forecast'. This is the single largest lever in the model and the optimism is unexplained.
challenges.answer: SG&A is now held in absolute terms at the 1H2026 annualised run-rate of about Rp21.7bn and rises with nominal inflation, no longer falling from FY2026E to FY2027E; the contradictory sentence is rewritten. No cost programme is assumed and the observed FY2025A-to-1H2026 cut is the only reduction in the base.

challenges.challenge: The model's own FY2022A line shows a 62.7% gross margin, 22.4% opex and a 44.6% EBIT margin (Rp13.79bn on Rp30.9bn), yet the bull caps at 50% gross margin and 36% opex for a v0 of Rp18.1, only +37% on a Rp13.2 base, so no scenario tests even a partial return to the economics the same brands earned. Worse, the bull narrative promises 'a change of control at a negotiated premium produces a tender offer for the minority' but its shocks are growth, margin and opex only: the tender offer carries zero weight. The file's largest single value driver is excluded from every scenario.
challenges.answer: The tender offer is deleted from the bull narrative: the bull is explicitly operating-only and the control event sits in section 5 with no weight. The bull shocks are widened toward the FY2022A economics (gross margin up seven points to 50%, opex down eleven points) and mirrored in the bear.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says the fixed base keeps 'SG&A above 80% of revenue' and that the company 'burns its Rp32.7bn cash balance and returns for equity at a discount to book', but the bear shocks only add +6pp to opex_pct (48% long-run, not 80%) and share_change is 0.0 in all three scenarios, so the dilutive raise is nowhere in the model. The bear lands at v0 Rp11.3 / TP 13, only 14% below base and 4.4x the DCF's Rp3.0. The spread is mechanical (+/-8pp growth, +/-5pp margin, -/+6pp opex) and tests neither named mechanism.
challenges.answer: The bear now matches its narrative: opex plus eleven points takes the ratio to about four fifths of sales at the FY2027E base, and the narrative is rewritten to the model. The dilutive equity raise cannot be shocked inside the mirrored-scenario engine, so it is disclosed in section 5 as additional downside outside the bear target; the SELL survives the bull at full weight.

challenges.challenge: The report flags D&A of Rp2.89bn against Rp62.8bn of net plant (4.6%) but then models Rp4.07bn and leaves the gap as a disclosure item. D&A is added back in FCFF, so it has no effect on the DCF at all; the consequence sits in the P/B leg, whose book equity of Rp111.9bn includes the plant that earns a 3% terminal EBIT margin (Rp2.17bn). An impairment to earning value at 5-7x EBIT would cut book by roughly Rp40bn, halve the P/B leg and take about Rp4 off the target, and no scenario carries it.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states plainly that D&A is added back in FCFF and does not touch the DCF cash flows, and that the forecast uses the filed run-rate. The plant impairment is disclosed in section 5 as cutting the book behind the P/B leg and removing several rupiah per share; the engine cannot restate book inside a scenario, and we say so rather than leave the gap implicit.

challenges.challenge: Every load-bearing financial cites [S0] and cov_fetch returns 'no archived text for S0', so none of the figures the valuation turns on - 1H2026 revenue Rp13.48bn, gross profit Rp5.98bn, SG&A Rp10.9bn, D&A Rp2.89bn, cash Rp32.7bn, equity Rp111.9bn, receivables Rp8.25bn, inventory Rp4.58bn, FY2022A gross margin 67% - can be traced by a reader. The source set contains no LK, no annual report and no prospectus, and the report itself says it could not open the LK notes. That is the entire evidence base of an initiation carrying an -82% call.
challenges.answer: Accepted as an evidence gap we could not close: repeated registry searches and the company IR pages produced no readable LK, annual report or prospectus, and idx.co.id is refused by design. We archived the company export coverage (S8) and disclose in sections 3, 6 and 7 that the LK notes are missing and that the load-bearing lines come from the data pack (S0). No source was invented.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 attributes excise, retail-sale restrictions on the highest-proof categories and local-content and labelling rules to [S7], and section 5 repeats the excise exposure. S7 (detik, 1 November 2023) contains no referral to cukai, excise or retail restrictions; it reports only the UMA notice and the 200% surge to Rp406. Section 2's claim that Bali distribution is 'contested by imported spirits at higher price points and by the national brewer's beer portfolio' cites [S5], which says only 'increasingly competitive global market'. Industry structure is asserted rather than sourced.
challenges.answer: Removed the false S7 attribution: S7 is now cited only for the unusual-market-activity notice and the 200% surge. Excise, retail restrictions, local-content and labelling rules and the Bali on-premise competitive claim are explicitly labelled analyst judgment, with the absence of an archived tariff or regulation stated.

challenges.challenge: The three methods use three different denominators without disclosure: the DCF is FY2026E-forward while EV/Sales is applied to FY2025A trough revenue (metric Rp12.91bn, giving Rp3.76/share). At the same 0.864x on FY2026E revenue of Rp29.04bn the method gives EV Rp25.1bn less net cash Rp29.1bn, a negative equity value, so the 10% weight is being carried by the denominator choice. More broadly, a ten-year DCF whose per-share value moves only Rp2.80 to Rp3.39 across +/-100bp of WACC and g is not doing DCF work: Rp29.2bn of the Rp32.4bn equity value is the net-cash bridge, so '70% weight on the only method with a defensible denominator' is really 70% weight on cash minus burn.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses each denominator: DCF forward from FY2026E, EV/Sales on FY2025A trough revenue with the effect of using FY2026E revenue stated, and P/B on the 30 June 2026 interim book. It also states that the DCF enterprise value is negative and the per-share result zero, so the DCF is a cash-minus-burn calculation.

challenges.challenge: Two statements in the crux paragraph are not supported by the model. First, the extreme_call justification says the price implies 'roughly seventy-five times FY2026E sales': enterprise value is Rp932.8bn - 29.2bn = Rp903.6bn against FY2026E revenue of Rp29.04bn, which is 31.1x (70x is FY2025A revenue), so the multiple is mislabelled by 2.4x. Second, section 4 says 'the reverse DCF does not produce a lower discount rate that closes the gap', but model.reverse_dcf.available is false with 'price not bracketed', so it did not run. Terminal capex of Rp3.62bn also sits below D&A of Rp5.07bn at 4% perpetual growth with a terminal ROE of 3%, and the card's implied-exit-multiple test is nowhere stated.
challenges.answer: qc_justifications.extreme_call now says thirty-one times FY2026E revenue (about seventy times FY2025A) instead of seventy-five times FY2026E; section 4 states the reverse DCF did not bracket the price rather than claim a result; terminal capex is set equal to terminal D&A with the reconciliation stated, and the implied exit test is added.

challenges.challenge: Unit and vintage errors in the numbers a reader checks first: the IPO offered 'IDR1,180.0bn shares' (S6 says 1.18bn), the controller holds 'IDR6,633.4bn shares' (S2 says 6,633,434,000, i.e. 6.63bn) and 'equity of IDR116.4bn over IDR10,721.8bn shares' (10.72bn). Book equity is Rp116.4bn (FY2025A) in section 4 but Rp111.9bn (30 June 2026) in the model; debt is 'IDR3.8bn' in section 3 against Rp3.5bn in the assumptions; and the 'IDR38.4bn cash pile' of sections 3 and 5 is the FY2025A balance while the valuation uses Rp32.7bn, even though cash is called the clock on the whole thesis. S4, fetched 11 November, shows Rp100 with a prior close of Rp101 and a Rp1,007.9bn market cap against the Rp87 price of 6 November.
challenges.answer: Share counts are in millions (1,180.0m IPO shares, 6,633.4m controller shares); the valuation uses one balance-sheet vintage, 30 June 2026, and annual figures are labelled FY2025A where used; the traded price is dated 6 November 2026 and the interim cash decline is stated without mixing vintages.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the book-value cross-check 'diverges from the DCF by an order of magnitude and the divergence is informative rather than a defect', but the divergence is 17.7x, i.e. +1,673%, and the lint still fires because the section never names it. The paragraph explains why book value is the higher number but not whether a 5.135x book multiple is appropriate; the divergence is averaged into the blend rather than resolved. The report also sits at 2,852 words against the house floor of 3,500 for an initiation, and the missing length is exactly the valuation method reconciliation.
challenges.answer: The 1,673% divergence is named in words and resolved by reweighting rather than averaging: P/B cut to 10% on the peer median, DCF at 80%, and the positive value attributed explicitly to the cross-checks. The report is now 4,710 words with the owner-earnings bridge, denominator reconciliation and terminal-capex test.

missing_bull_case.note: Two gaps. The bull case is operating-only (+8pp growth, +5pp margin, -6pp opex) even though its own narrative promises a tender offer at a negotiated premium, so the file's biggest value driver carries zero weight. And no scenario tests the FY2022A P&L the same brands actually earned (62.7% gross margin, 22.4% opex, 44.6% EBIT margin, EBIT Rp13.79bn on Rp30.9bn); the bull caps at 50% and 36%. Both are understated.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative's two named mechanisms are not in the model: SG&A 'above 80% of revenue' becomes a +6pp shock (48% long-run) and the dilutive equity raise is share_change 0.0 in all scenarios. No impairment of the Rp62.8bn plant, whose book underpins the P/B leg, is carried anywhere. The bear TP of 13 is only 14% below base and 4.4x the DCF's Rp3.0, so the downside is not tested.

assumption_realism.note: The biggest single lever, SG&A, is modelled Rp9.2bn (31%) below FY2023A's actual Rp29.58bn at the same Rp39.2bn revenue, with no sourced cost programme, and it falls in absolute terms in FY2027E while revenue grows 35%. The FY2026E anchor is worse: 2Q26 revenue fell to Rp5.18bn (26.1% gross margin) from Rp8.29bn in 1Q26, yet the base holds 42% for the year and Rp29.04bn of revenue against the Rp27bn flat-half arithmetic the basis states.

evidence_and_citations.note: S0 carries every load-bearing financial and is not archived (cov_fetch: no archived text for S0); there is no LK, annual report or prospectus in the source set, and the report admits it could not open the LK notes. S3 does not contain the whisky/five-star-hotel shipment it is cited for, and S7 contains no excise or retail-restriction content. FY2023A noii of Rp39.75bn, the S6 warrants and the S2 block facts do check out.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 70%-weighted DCF produces Rp3.02 but the 20%-weighted P/B produces Rp53.6 and supplies Rp10.72 of the Rp13.21 blend, so the method the report itself calls structurally misleading sets the target. Its 5.135x is the average of a 1.587x peer median and an 'own five-year average' that is a 3-observation mean (n=3) including 18.60x at December 2025. EV/Sales uses FY2025A trough revenue while the DCF is FY2026E-forward, and the reverse DCF did not run.

bias_and_tone.note: The SELL itself is not bias: it survives a 100% bull weight, a doubled bear probability and the DCF bear, so the call is driven by base-case arithmetic, and that should be credited. Where the prose runs ahead of the evidence is the export ramp (a fabricated five-star-hotel shipment), the claim that Rp6.7bn daily traded value is 'speculation rather than liquidity' on a Rp933bn cap, and describing a 1,673% P/B divergence as 'informative rather than a defect' when that leg is 81% of the target.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The zero cost-link treatment is correct and well argued: no reviewed deck prices malt, glass, molasses or freight, so link1/link2 at zero avoids importing a commodity sensitivity the company does not have. COE 12.54% is inside the 11-13% IDR band, terminal g 4.0% is below long-run nominal GDP, and the peers used are the FOOD_BEVERAGE set. Only the peer-multiple choice, filed under valuation, is off.

conservatism_audit.note: Sourced-or-not, both directions: conservative and unsourced are gross margin 45% vs FY2023A's 62.7% and FY2022A's 67%, nwc 46% vs FY2025A's 87%, and tax stepping to 22% when the LK shows 7.3% effective in FY2023A; optimistic and unsourced are opex 42% vs 75%/22.4%, capex 3-5% vs FY2024A's 15.7% of revenue, and FY2026E revenue 7.7% above the stated arithmetic. The stack is large but it does not flip the rating, so it is a material rebuild rather than a fatal one.

calibration.note: The calibration gate is marked justified, but the justification rests on the inverted claim that 1H2026 had 'a weaker first quarter' - 1Q26 was the stronger quarter (Rp8.29bn, 55.8% gross margin) and 2Q26 collapsed to Rp5.18bn at 26.1%. FY+1 therefore does not reproduce the last actual at last-year prices on a sourced basis: it needs an unstated second-half recovery in both revenue (+15% h/h) and gross margin.

signoff.notes: Gates hold: facts and lint PASS, no engine blocking flags, all 14 FATAL/MATERIAL red-team challenges answered on substance (C9 evidence gap accepted, not papered over), QC round 2 PASS with a neutral bias note (judge confidence 0.94). Method fits the FOOD_BEVERAGE/compounder card: WACC 12.5% inside the IDR 11-13% band, terminal g 4% at/below nominal GDP, no-fade ruled out, owner-earnings bridge given, multiple-survival test run and honestly reported undefined on a negative EBIT denominator; the 80/10/10 weights are a justified departure because P/E and EV/EBITDA have no usable denominator. Most-likely, not most-cautious: base revenue is anchored to the filed 1H26/2Q26 path (QC recompute 23.85 vs 23.88, 0.1% gap), SG&A held at the 1H26 absolute run-rate (Rp21.7bn, already below FY2025A Rp29.3bn, i.e. generous), long-run GM 45% is the 1H26 level, bull mirrors the bear, and 100% bull weight still gives Rp8.64 (about -90%) so the SELL does not rest on conservatism; unmodelled dilution and impairment both cut against the SELL and are disclosed. Industry-coherent: the sector SELL/REDUCE names are the negative-cash-economics microcaps (BEEF -84%, FORE -48%, ROTI -22%); STRK is extreme because the price is about 32x net cash and 38x forward sales, while the Rp4 target is essentially net cash per share (Rp2.7) plus a thin asset floor. No shared-input tilt: STRK zero-links the agri decks and the batch is mixed BUY/SELL/HOLD. bias.note: Base is anchored to the filed quarterly path, not a default haircut: FY2026E revenue Rp23.88bn vs my rebuild 13.479 + 2x5.185 = 23.85 (0.1% gap) [S0]; SG&A held flat in absolute terms at the 1H2026 annualised Rp21.7bn, which is generous to profit; the bull was widened to +7pp gross margin mirroring the bear, bull tp Rp8.64, so a 100% bull weight still gives about -90% and the SELL does not depend on conservatism. findings.finding: The crux paragraph renders the market capitalisation as 932,799,693,894.0 with no currency or unit while the report is in IDR bn; the value is correct (Rp87 x 10,721.8m shares) but it is the same units family as round-1 Q5.

Section 5 and the bull narrative call the 52% long-run gross margin halfway between the 45% base and the 62.7% FY2023A actual; 45+7pp is 52%, about two fifths of that span (the midpoint would be 53.9%). The error is conservative and immaterial to the call.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +158.8pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The FY2025A base is a negative-EBITDA trough: revenue of Rp12.9bn against a cost base built for three times that volume produced an EBITDA of -Rp25.9bn [S0], so any normalisation prints as a triple-digit percentage move off a negative denominator. FY2026E is not a forecast drift either: 1H2026 revenue of Rp13.48bn and gross profit of Rp5.98bn were filed, and the second half priced at the 2Q26 exit run-rate carries the year to roughly Rp23.8bn at a gross margin in the mid-thirties [S0]. The gate is measuring recovery from a trough, which is the path the filings show.

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves +8.5pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +8.5pp from FY2026E to the long run is the absorption recovery, not a margin expansion assumption. Gross margin was 3.9% in FY2025A and 44.3% in 1H2026 on the same plant [S0]; FY2026E is 36.5% only because the second quarter's 26.1% exit margin is carried through the second half, and the path then recovers to 45% as volume rebuilds over the fixed asset base, still 22 points below the 67% the same brands earned in FY2022A [S0]. No archived source quantifies the freight and rebate of the export and sub-distributor channel [S5][S8], so that cost sits inside the margin path as judgment rather than as a sourced line.

flags.message: a.opex_pct moves -43.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The -41pp is not a cost-cutting assumption: SG&A is fixed-heavy distribution, listing and promotion spend, and we hold the absolute line at the 1H2026 annualised run-rate of about Rp21.7bn, rising only with nominal inflation [S0]. The ratio falls because revenue rises from Rp23.8bn to Rp48.9bn, not because costs are cut. FY2023A's 75% ratio at Rp39.3bn of revenue [S0] sits above our path because the current cost base is already lower: SG&A was Rp29.6bn in FY2023A and Rp29.3bn in FY2025A but only Rp10.9bn in the 1H2026 filing, an annualised Rp21.7bn.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves +3.7pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +3.7pp from FY2026E to the long run is a maintenance-capex normalisation, not a build cycle, and the S0 arithmetic answers the flag on its own: the Rp66.3bn plant was commissioned in FY2023A and capex had fallen to Rp0.15bn by FY2025A [S0], so there is no second build to fund. The terminal ratio is deliberately set equal to terminal D&A so that a business growing 4% a year is not modelled with a shrinking asset base; capex below depreciation at positive growth would be an internal inconsistency. The path stays far below the 61.9% capex-to-revenue of the FY2022A-FY2023A build years [S0].

flags.message: expected return -96%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the call: SG&A at 81% of 1H2026 sales and 75% at the FY2023A revenue peak [S0], a gross margin that must cover that structure, and 10,721.8m shares against the interim book and cash of the 30 June 2026 balance sheet [S0]. Today's price implies an enterprise value of roughly thirty-eight times FY2026E revenue (about seventy times FY2025A revenue) and no plausible margin path can fill it: at the FY2030E revenue and margin in this model the business barely reaches operating breakeven. The reverse DCF did not bracket the price - the implied value sits outside the solver's range and is reported as unavailable - which is itself the answer: no discount rate close to the cost of capital reconciles the price with the cash flows. It is pricing a change of control at PT Beruntung Berkat Sejahtera for the 61.87% held by PT Barito Mas Sukses [S2], which is why the stock doubled in October 2026; section 5 treats that as event risk, not value.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.1}
flags.justification: The blend is 80% DCF, 10% P/B and 10% EV/Sales against the industry default of 60% DCF, 30% P/E and 10% EV/EBITDA [S0]. Both default earnings legs are unusable rather than merely unattractive: EPS is negative in every forecast year of this model and EBITDA is negative through FY2029E [S0], so those multiples have no meaningful denominator in the period the target covers, and a trailing multiple on a collapsed year would import the same speculation the report argues against. P/B replaces them as an asset floor struck on the 30 June 2026 interim book, EV/Sales is kept as a scale check on the last audited sales line, and both are held at ten per cent so neither can drive a target the cash flows do not support. Section 4 states the substitution.
